paginas.texto: Maya read that the aurora would be visible on Saturday, and the whole school started planning at once.
'We are going to walk to the mirador,' said Ingrid. 'We are going to leave at eight and we are NOT going to be late.'
Oliver was going to bring the guitar. Diego was going to bring the microphone. Kili was going to bring himself.
They needed warm clothes, because at the top of the hill the wind never asks how you feel about it.
On Saturday at eight they left. At eight fifteen Diego went back for the microphone he had left at home.
The walk was long and dark and cold, and nobody said one word about turning round.
At the top they waited. Nothing happened. It was cold. Somebody said the word 'chocolate' and everybody agreed.
And then the sky turned green. Not a little green. All of it, from the sea to the mountain.
Diego did not record anything. He said afterwards that he forgot, but Maya says he chose to watch.
They walked home very late and very happy, and on Monday nobody could explain it to the people who had stayed in bed.
